hints: Look in two places, the bonds holding atoms together inside a polyatomic ion, and the bond holding that ion to its counter ion.
Remember that $\text{NH}_4^+$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ both contain a dative bond where one atom supplies both shared electrons.
Check which compound leaves you with ordinary shared electron covalent bonds inside plus an ionic attraction outside, with no dative bond needed to make it.
walkthrough:
**Understand the three bond types**

Think of ionic as transfer and attraction between opposite ions. Think of covalent as normal sharing, one electron from each atom. Think of coordinate, also called dative, as sharing where one atom gives both electrons.

Rule to test:
$$\text{need ionic (between ions) + covalent (normal sharing) + NO coordinate}$$

**Spot the coordinate bonds first**

$\text{NH}_4^+$ is made when $\text{NH}_3$ donates its lone pair to $\text{H}^+$. That N to H bond is coordinate. $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ is a dimer where terminal Cl atoms donate lone pairs to bridge to the other Al. Those Al-Cl bridge bonds are coordinate.

$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{NH}_4^+ \text{ (one N-H is dative)}$$

**Test the remaining two compounds**

$\text{MgCl}_2$ is simply $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ with $2\text{Cl}^-$. It is ionic only, with no polyatomic ion to provide covalent bonds. $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ separates into $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$ and $\text{Na}^+$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COONa(s)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- + \text{Na}^+ \text{ (ionic part)}$$

**Confirm covalent inside ethanoate**

Inside $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$, all bonds like C-H, C-C and C-O are normal covalent bonds with one electron from each atom. No atom had to donate both electrons, so there is no coordinate bond. That gives ionic plus covalent only.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ has covalent Al-Cl bonds plus coordinate Al-Cl bridge bonds from Cl lone pairs to Al, but it has no ionic bonding. It fails on both conditions.
options.B: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ has ionic bonding between $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$, and normal covalent bonds (C-H, C-C, C-O) inside the ethanoate ion. There is no coordinate bond.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{MgCl}_2$ is ionic between $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ only. There is no discrete covalent molecule or polyatomic ion, so it lacks covalent bonding.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ does have ionic ($\text{NH}_4^+$ to $\text{Cl}^-$) and covalent (N-H) bonding, but it also has coordinate bonding because $\text{NH}_4^+$ is formed by a dative bond from N to $\text{H}^+$. The question says not coordinate.
